notes: BLS OOH pay is for all workers in an occupation (any experience level), May 2025, nominal dollars. The 10th percentile is the closest OOH gives to a starting wage.

College Scorecard earnings are medians for graduates working and not enrolled, measured in 2022–2023 and inflation-adjusted to 2024 dollars. 'Pell' medians are for graduates who received a Pell Grant, a proxy for lower-income students.
NY Fed outcomes by major are for 2024 (American Community Survey). Early career = ages 22–27, mid-career = ages 35–45; wages are for full-time workers with only a bachelor's degree.
Fields marked "derived": true are computed from published values using the stated method. Fields marked "assumption": true are modeling choices for the author to confirm.
Scorecard rows with fewer than 100 graduates are left out because their medians are unstable.

earningsByCollegeTier.description: Median earnings of graduates by college tier and credential: mean of program-level medians weighted by the number of graduates with earnings. Tiers use the same definitions as net-price.json.
earningsByCollegeTier.fields: EARN_MDN_1YR, EARN_MDN_5YR weighted by EARN_COUNT_WNE_1YR / EARN_COUNT_WNE_5YR

definitions.unemploymentRate: Percent, recent graduates aged 22–27 with a bachelor's degree or higher
definitions.underemploymentRate: Percent working in jobs that typically do not require a college degree

recentGradWages.description: Annual wages of full-time workers aged 22–27 who are not enrolled in school, 2025, in 2025 dollars.

entrySalary.rule: Degree and certificate roles start at the Scorecard 1-year national median for the role's scorecardLink, multiplied by collegeTierRatio. Roles without a scorecardLink start at the OOH 10th percentile (p10Annual, or p10Hourly × hours worked).
entrySalary.note: The OOH 10th percentile covers all workers in the occupation and is used only as a proxy for a starting wage.

collegeTierRatio.note: Includes field-mix and selection effects, so it overstates the effect of the college itself. Consider shrinking toward 1.0.

annualGrowth.note: The 1-year and 5-year medians come from different graduating cohorts measured in the same years, so this is a cross-sectional estimate of early-career growth.

hoursPerYearFullTime.note: 40 hours × 52 weeks, the convention BLS uses to annualize hourly wages. Part-time teen jobs need their own hours assumption.
